Formulation  
Patient recently returned from travel to Thailand, presenting with severe headache, fever, generalized red itchy blanching rash, and muscle aches without photophobia or neck stiffness. Clinical concern includes potential viral illnesses related to mosquito bites (eg, dengue), with differential diagnosis including meningitis considered but less likely given absence of neck pain, photophobia, and non-blanching rash. Urgent face-to-face examination and blood tests recommended to rule out serious infections. Patient’s recent travel and exposure are predisposing and precipitating factors. Protective factors include patient insight and engagement with care advice.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Possible serious viral infection post travel presenting with systemic symptoms  
- Patient Goal(s): To be evaluated urgently in person to determine cause and receive appropriate treatment  
- Clinical Goal(s): To perform clinical examination, diagnostic investigations (blood tests), and initiate treatment or referral as needed  
- Actions (Patient): Attend urgent face-to-face assessment at clinic hub as soon as possible; seek emergency care if condition worsens  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Arrange urgent in-person clinical evaluation today; perform physical examination and relevant investigations; refer to hospital if indicated
